papers.title: Mpox knowledge levels and associated factors among MSM in Chongqing and Chengdu, China
papers.abstract: Monkeypox (Mpox) has become a major public health threat globally, with men who have sex with men (MSM) being the primary affected population. In China, the mpox epidemic has spread to multiple provinces, but regional research on MSM in the Chongqing-Chengdu urban agglomeration is lacking. A cross-sectional study was conducted among MSM in Chongqing and Chengdu from August to December 2024 using convenience sampling via community-based organizations. A self-designed questionnaire was used to collect data on socio-demographic characteristics, sexual behaviors, HIV-related status, mpox information attention and knowledge level. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with mpox knowledge awareness. A total of 514 valid questionnaires were collected. The overall awareness rate of mpox knowledge was 49.6%, with a median knowledge score of 9.0 (IQR: 6.0, 12.0). Participants demonstrated high accuracy in responses related to preventive measures (82.1%) and sexual transmission routes (80.0%), whereas correct responses were lower for the incubation period (53.5%) and universal susceptibility (56.6%). The primary source of mpox information was the internet and social media (49.8%). Multivariable analysis showed that having a college education or higher (aOR = 2.47, 95% CI 1.32–4.60), identifying as homosexual (aOR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.01–2.44), absence of group sex in the past year (aOR = 2.55, 95% CI 1.09–5.93), travel to mpox-endemic countries in the past year (aOR = 4.18, 95% CI 1.32–4.60) and actively seeking mpox-related information (aOR = 3.40, 95% CI 2.03–5.71) were independent factors associated with higher mpox knowledge levels. The level of mpox knowledge awareness among MSM in Chongqing and Chengdu was moderate, characterized by an uneven distribution of knowledge. Information acquisition was predominantly through digital channels with insufficient professional input. Targeted health education strategies should be developed for key populations, and an integrated promotion model of “professional personnel + authoritative new media” should be constructed to improve the effectiveness of mpox prevention and control in this population.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed Mpox knowledge levels and associated factors among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Chongqing and Chengdu, China. A cross-sectional survey conducted from August to December 2024 collected 514 valid questionnaires through convenience sampling. The overall awareness rate of Mpox knowledge was 49.6%, with a median knowledge score of 9.0. papers.title: New Crossover Monkeypox Disease Mathematical Model Based on Fractal Fractional Caputo-Katugampola Derivative: Numerical Solutions
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel crossover epidemiological model for the transmission dynamics of monkeypox, integrating fractal-fractional Caputo-Katugampola derivatives with stochastic perturbations driven by fractional Brownian motion. The proposed framework captures complex memory, hereditary, and environmental effects within two temporally distinct regimes: a deterministic fractal-fractional phase and a stochastic fractional-order phase. We establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions using the Perov fixed-point theorem within generalized Banach spaces. To numerically solve the system, we construct a $\kappa$-nonstandard finite difference scheme and adapted modified Euler-Maruyama method adapted to the fractional stochastic setting.Sensitivity and bifurcation analyses reveal that transmission-related parameters are the primary drivers of disease dynamics, leading to the emergence of a forward bifurcation that marks the transition from disease-free to endemic states. Numerical simulations, calibrated with real outbreak data from the United States, demonstrate excellent agreement and highlight the critical role of memory and stochasticity in shaping infection trajectories. The results underscore the utility of fractal-fractional stochastic modeling for improving predictive power and informing targeted intervention strategies in emerging epidemics.
papers.journal: European Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics

papers.title: Atypical Presentation of Mpox as Acute Tonsillitis: A Case Report from the United Arab Emirates
papers.abstract: Mpox typically presents with a prodrome of fever and lymphadenopathy followed by a characteristic vesiculopustular rash. Mpox may present with atypical manifestations, including isolated oropharyngeal, anogenital, and mucosal involvement preceding cutaneous lesions. Recognition of these atypical phenotypes is essential to avoid diagnostic delay and limit secondary transmission, particularly in regions such as the United Arab Emirates and the wider Gulf where published descriptions of atypical presentations remain limited. A previously healthy 28-year-old man in the United Arab Emirates presented with a two-day history of severe sore throat and painful swallowing that prevented oral intake. Examination revealed bilateral erythematous palatine tonsils with cryptic exudate, an edematous uvula, and pharyngeal erythema. There was no stridor or respiratory distress. Inflammatory markers were elevated (WBC count 14.0 × 109/L; CRP 102 mg/L). Computed tomography of the neck demonstrated bulky, heterogeneous palatine tonsils with significant narrowing of the oropharyngeal lumen and reactive cervical lymphadenopathy; the radiologist’s impression raised the possibility of evolving abscess. A working diagnosis of acute bacterial tonsillitis was made, and intravenous ceftriaxone and dexamethasone were commenced. On hospital day 2, mild non-specific cutaneous lesions appeared, progressing on day 3 to a characteristic vesiculopustular eruption involving the face, trunk, palms, and genital area. Throat culture, finalised on day 4, yielded normal upper respiratory tract flora with no beta-haemolytic streptococci. Real-time PCR on a skin lesion swab confirmed Mpox virus infection (cycle threshold 12). The patient was isolated, transferred to a designated facility on hospital day 9, and discharged home on 11 January 2026 after a total of 27 days from initial admission. A structured post-discharge telephone follow-up on 12 January 2026 confirmed sustained clinical recovery with full lesion resolution and no recurrent symptoms. Mpox can present initially as severe pharyngotonsillitis with significant oropharyngeal luminal narrowing, mimicking acute bacterial infection and preceding the appearance of skin lesions by several days, even in young, immunocompetent patients without recognised epidemiological risk factors. Clinicians should consider Mpox in patients with severe pharyngotonsillitis, particularly when bacterial cultures are negative or when even subtle cutaneous changes appear during admission, to enable timely isolation and appropriate management.

Mpox may present with atypical manifestations, including isolated oropharyngeal, anogenital, and mucosal involvement preceding cutaneous lesions. Recognition of these atypical phenotypes is essential to avoid diagnostic delay and limit secondary transmission, particularly in regions such as the United Arab Emirates and the wider Gulf where published descriptions of atypical presentations remain limited. A previously healthy 28-year-old man in the United Arab Emirates presented with a two-day history of severe sore throat and painful swallowing that prevented oral intake. Examination revealed bilateral erythematous palatine tonsils with cryptic exudate, an edematous uvula, and pharyngeal erythema. There was no stridor or respiratory distress. Inflammatory markers were elevated (WBC count 14.0 × 109/L; CRP 102 mg/L). Computed tomography of the neck demonstrated bulky, heterogeneous palatine tonsils with significant narrowing of the oropharyngeal lumen and reactive cervical lymphadenopathy; the radiologist’s impression raised the possibility of evolving abscess. A working diagnosis of acute bacterial tonsillitis was made, and intravenous ceftriaxone and dexamethasone were commenced. On hospital day 2, mild non-specific cutaneous lesions appeared, progressing on day 3 to a characteristic vesiculopustular eruption involving the face, trunk, palms, and genital area. Throat culture, finalised on day 4, yielded normal upper respiratory tract flora with no beta-haemolytic streptococci. Real-time PCR on a skin lesion swab confirmed Mpox virus infection (cycle threshold 12). The patient was isolated, transferred to a designated facility on hospital day 9, and discharged home on 11 January 2026 after a total of 27 days from initial admission. A structured post-discharge telephone follow-up on 12 January 2026 confirmed sustained clinical recovery with full lesion resolution and no recurrent symptoms. Mpox can present initially as severe pharyngotonsillitis with significant oropharyngeal luminal narrowing, mimicking acute bacterial infection and preceding the appearance of skin lesions by several days, even in young, immunocompetent patients without recognised epidemiological risk factors. Clinicians should consider Mpox in patients with severe pharyngotonsillitis, particularly when bacterial cultures are negative or when even subtle cutaneous changes appear during admission, to enable timely isolation and appropriate management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report an atypical presentation of mpox as acute tonsillitis to highlight diagnostic challenges in regions with limited published descriptions of such manifestations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a case report of a previously healthy 28-year-old man in the United Arab Emirates who presented with severe sore throat and painful swallowing.
analysis.methods: The patient was evaluated with inflammatory markers, computed tomography of the neck, throat culture, and real-time PCR on a skin lesion swab to confirm mpox virus infection.
analysis.main_results: The patient initially presented with bilateral erythematous palatine tonsils with cryptic exudate, elevated inflammatory markers, and imaging suggestive of abscess; skin lesions appeared later, and PCR confirmed mpox with a cycle threshold of 12.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that mpox can initially mimic acute bacterial tonsillitis, even in young immunocompetent patients without risk factors, and emphasized the importance of recognizing atypical presentations to avoid diagnostic delay.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform clinicians to consider mpox in severe pharyngotonsillitis cases, especially with negative bacterial cultures or subtle cutaneous changes, to enable timely isolation and management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is low due to the single-case design, which limits generalizability, though the detailed clinical and laboratory findings provide robust documentation of this atypical presentation.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 28-year-old man in the United Arab Emirates who initially presented with severe acute tonsillitis, mimicking bacterial infection, before developing characteristic mpox skin lesions. Diagnostic workup included elevated inflammatory markers, imaging suggestive of abscess, negative throat culture, and PCR-confirmed mpox virus infection. The authors highlight that mpox can present as isolated oropharyngeal involvement preceding cutaneous lesions, even in immunocompetent patients without risk factors, emphasizing the need for clinicians to consider mpox in atypical presentations to avoid diagnostic delay and enable timely isolation.

papers.abstract_zh: 猴痘 通常表现为发烧和淋巴结肿大的前驱症状,随后出现特征性水疱脓疱性皮疹。猴痘 可能出现非典型表现,包括孤立的口咽部、肛门生殖器和粘膜受累,先于皮肤病变。识别这些非典型表型对于避免诊断延迟和限制继发性 传播 至关重要,特别是在阿拉伯联合酋长国和更广泛的海湾等地区,这些地区已发表的非典型表现描述仍然有限。阿拉伯联合酋长国一名原本健康的 28 岁男性出现了两天严重喉咙痛和吞咽疼痛导致无法进食的病史。检查发现双侧腭扁桃体红斑,有隐秘渗出物,悬雍垂水肿,咽部红斑。没有喘鸣或呼吸困难。炎症标志物升高(WBC 计数 14.0 × 109/L;CRP 102 mg/L)。颈部计算机断层扫描显示腭扁桃体体积庞大、异质,口咽腔明显变窄,颈部淋巴结肿大;放射科医生的印象提出了发展脓肿的可能性。制作了急性细菌性扁桃体炎工作诊断,并开始静脉注射头孢曲松和地塞米松。住院第 2 天,出现轻度非特异性皮肤损害,第 3 天进展为特征性水疱脓疱疹,累及面部、躯干、手掌和生殖器区域。第 4 天完成的咽喉培养结果显示上呼吸道菌群正常,没有发现 β 溶血性链球菌。皮肤病变拭子的实时 PCR 证实了 猴痘病毒 感染(循环阈值 12)。该患者在入院第 9 天被隔离并转移至指定机构,并于 2026 年 1 月 11 日出院回家,距入院总共 27 天。2026 年 1 月 12 日进行的结构化出院后电话随访证实,患者持续临床康复,病变完全消退,并且没有复发症状。猴痘 最初可表现为严重的咽扁桃体炎,伴有明显的口咽腔狭窄,类似于急性细菌感染,并且在出现皮肤病变之前几天,即使是在没有公认的流行病学危险因素的年轻、免疫功能正常的患者中也是如此。临床医生应在患有严重咽扁桃体炎的患者中考虑使用猴痘,特别是当细菌培养呈阴性或入院期间甚至出现细微的皮肤变化时,以便及时隔离和适当的治疗。

papers.title: Vaccine safety surveillance during an mpox outbreak, Germany, June 2022 to February 2024
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND In May 2022, first cases of mpox clade IIb were detected in Germany, and MVA-BN vaccine was available from June 2022 onwards. Vaccination has been recommended by the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) since June 2022 to contain monkeypox virus infection and prevent disease. AIM Our primary aim was to evaluate the safety of the mpox vaccine Jynneos (modified Vaccinia Ankara, Bavaria-Nordic, MVA-BN) after the rollout of the vaccination campaign in Germany from June 2022 to February 2024; a secondary aim was to describe mpox cases and vaccinations. METHODS To identify cases and persons with adverse events following immunisation (AEFIs), we used existing surveillance systems. A voluntary system was implemented in June 2022 to monitor mpox vaccination. We performed a descriptive analysis of cases, vaccinations, individual case safety reports (ICSRs) and AEFIs. RESULTS Until 29 February 2024, 3,807 mpox cases were notified (data retrieved July 2024). According to the voluntary mpox vaccination monitoring, a total of 78,739 mpox vaccine doses of Jynneos were administered. A search of the national AEFI database identified 32 ICSRs, of which seven were serious. A total of 87 AEFIs were reported, most of which were local or systemic reactions that are generally associated with vaccination. The overall adverse event reporting rate adjusted for missing information on vaccine utilisation in one of 16 federal states was 98.7 adverse events per 100,000 doses. CONCLUSION The safety profile of the MVA-BN vaccine was in line with the summary of product characteristics. No new safety signals were identified.

source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND In May 2022, first cases of mpox clade IIb were detected in Germany, and MVA-BN vaccine was available from June 2022 onwards. Vaccination has been recommended by the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) since June 2022 to contain monkeypox virus infection and prevent disease. AIM Our primary aim was to evaluate the safety of the mpox vaccine Jynneos (modified Vaccinia Ankara, Bavaria-Nordic, MVA-BN) after the rollout of the vaccination campaign in Germany from June 2022 to February 2024; a secondary aim was to describe mpox cases and vaccinations. METHODS To identify cases and persons with adverse events following immunisation (AEFIs), we used existing surveillance systems. A voluntary system was implemented in June 2022 to monitor mpox vaccination. We performed a descriptive analysis of cases, vaccinations, individual case safety reports (ICSRs) and AEFIs. RESULTS Until 29 February 2024, 3,807 mpox cases were notified (data retrieved July 2024). According to the voluntary mpox vaccination monitoring, a total of 78,739 mpox vaccine doses of Jynneos were administered. A search of the national AEFI database identified 32 ICSRs, of which seven were serious. A total of 87 AEFIs were reported, most of which were local or systemic reactions that are generally associated with vaccination. The overall adverse event reporting rate adjusted for missing information on vaccine utilisation in one of 16 federal states was 98.7 adverse events per 100,000 doses. CONCLUSION The safety profile of the MVA-BN vaccine was in line with the summary of product characteristics. No new safety signals were identified.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety of the mpox vaccine Jynneos (MVA-BN) in Germany from June 2022 to February 2024. papers.title: Branched C7-Substituted 7-Deaza-SAH Analogues Occupy the Entire SAM-Binding Pocket of Mpox Virus VP39 and Dengue Virus NS5 Methyltransferases
papers.abstract: Abstract Viral RNA-cap MTases are attractive targets for antiviral drug development. We previously identified C7-substituted 7-deaza-SAH analogues as potent inhibitors of the mpox virus 2′-O-MTase VP39. Here, we used structure-guided design to develop branched C7-substituted analogues intended to engage multiple hydrophobic regions of the VP39 SAM-binding pocket. The synthesized compounds were characterized using biochemical and crystallographic approaches. Several analogues effectively inhibited VP39, with the most potent compound displaying an IC 50 in the tens-of-nanomolar range. Crystal structures of VP39 in complex with STM1187 and STM1189 confirmed that the branched aromatic substituents extend towards hydrophobic regions adjacent to the SAM binding site. The precise ligand conformations were strongly influenced by linker geometry and the branching group’s mode of attachment. STM1078 also inhibited DENV3 NS5 MTase with submicromolar potency, and the complex’s structure revealed a conserved binding mode of the SAH-like core accompanied by conformational adaptability of the branched substituent. These results demonstrate how three-dimensional expansion from the 7-deaza position can generate potent inhibitors capable of binding structurally distinct viral MTases.

papers.title: High-resolution structure of the vaccinia virus phospholipase D-fold endonuclease K4.
papers.abstract: Vaccinia virus (VACV) is an orthopoxvirus closely related to mpox virus, which started global outbreaks in 2022. Poxvirus genomes are flanked by short, inverted complementary hairpin telomeres that feature mismatched bases and insertions essential for viral replication. In this context, a role of the late protein K4 has been proposed. K4 is present in the virion, is apparently non-essential and has a phospholipase D (PLD)-fold as has VACV F13 protein. It also shares fold and nuclease activity with its closest homologue, mammalian PLD3. We established an endonuclease activity against ssDNA and hairpin loops and bubbles in a dsDNA context while RNA is resistant to cleavage. The 2.4 Å cryo-EM structure of K4 shows an unusual octameric assembly, also present in solution. At low concentration, tetramers and dimers similar to the one of hPLD3 are also present. Despite its nuclease activity, in K4 a C-terminal extension blocks the DNA binding pockets. Using an inactive mutant, fortuitously, a DNA 19mer bound simultaneously to 2 sites of the octamer where it displaced the C-termini. DNA binding uses similar residues as the hPLD3 5'-exonuclease, despite different activities and orientations of the DNA. The role of K4 and the control of its activity by the observed auto-inhibition remain enigmatic.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the vaccinia virus protein K4, analyzing its structural and enzymatic properties using cryo-electron microscopy and biochemical assays.
analysis.methods: The researchers determined the 2.4 Å cryo-EM structure of K4 and assessed its endonuclease activity against single-stranded DNA, hairpin loops, and bubbles in double-stranded DNA, while testing resistance to RNA cleavage.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究重点关注牛痘病毒蛋白 K4,利用冷冻电子显微镜和生化检测分析其结构和酶学特性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员确定了 K4 的 2.4 Å 冷冻电镜结构,并评估了其针对单链 DNA、发夹环和双链 DNA 中的气泡的核酸内切酶活性,同时测试了对 RNA 切割的抵抗力。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 K4 的结构和活性解释为痘病毒蛋白中独一无二的,并指出它通过 C 末端延伸进行自动抑制,并且尽管活性不同,但其 DNA 结合机制类似于 hPLD3。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现促进了对痘病毒酶机制的理解,可能为针对 正痘病毒 保守结构特征的 抗病毒药物 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管 K4 的确切生物学作用及其调控仍然是个谜,但由于高分辨率结构数据和直接生化测定,该研究的证据强度很高。

papers.title: Mathematical Analysis of Monkeypox Disease Using Fractional Delay Differential Equations and Vaccination Control
papers.abstract: This study presents a fractional-order model for the transmission dynamics of Monkeypox, formulated using Caputo fractional order delay differential equations. The model incorporates two types of delays: one representing diagnostic delays in humans and the other associated with rodent populations. The proposed framework further integrates vaccination strategies and assesses the demand for clinical care. Analytically, the existence, uniqueness, non-negativity, and boundedness of solutions have been established. The basic reproduction number R0 has been derived, and a sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters most influencing R0. Specifically, the transmission rates β1 and β3, and the parameter ω1 exhibit the strongest influence, whereas the γ has the least impact. Furthermore, the stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria has been investigated using the curve-switching method in the presence of time delays. Additionally, graphical simulations demonstrated the effects of delays, vaccination rates, and fractional orders. The results indicate that increasing the vaccination rate reduces the infected population, and large values of the delay parameters of the model produce slower disease trajectories and lower infection peaks at fixed time as compared to delays with lower values. This reflects a slower system response rather than the actual situation. These findings highlight the sensitivity of disease progression to delays.
papers.journal: European Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics

papers.title_zh: 使用分数阶时滞微分方程和 疫苗接种 控制对猴痘病进行数学分析
papers.source_body_en: This study presents a fractional-order model for the transmission dynamics of Monkeypox, formulated using Caputo fractional order delay differential equations. The model incorporates two types of delays: one representing diagnostic delays in humans and the other associated with rodent populations. The proposed framework further integrates vaccination strategies and assesses the demand for clinical care. Analytically, the existence, uniqueness, non-negativity, and boundedness of solutions have been established. The basic reproduction number R0 has been derived, and a sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters most influencing R0. Specifically, the transmission rates β1 and β3, and the parameter ω1 exhibit the strongest influence, whereas the γ has the least impact. Furthermore, the stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria has been investigated using the curve-switching method in the presence of time delays. Additionally, graphical simulations demonstrated the effects of delays, vaccination rates, and fractional orders. The results indicate that increasing the vaccination rate reduces the infected population, and large values of the delay parameters of the model produce slower disease trajectories and lower infection peaks at fixed time as compared to delays with lower values. This reflects a slower system response rather than the actual situation. These findings highlight the sensitivity of disease progression to delays.
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究提出了猴痘 传播 动力学的分数阶模型,该模型使用 Caputo 分数阶延迟微分方程制定。该模型包含两种类型的延迟:一种代表人类的诊断延迟,另一种与啮齿动物种群相关。提出的框架进一步整合了 疫苗接种 策略并评估临床护理的需求。解析上,解的存在性、唯一性、非负性和有界性已成立。基本再生数 R0 已得出,敏感性分析确定了对 R0 影响最大的参数。具体而言,传播 速率β1 和β3 以及参数ω1 的影响最强,而γ 的影响最小。此外,在存在时间延迟的情况下,使用曲线切换方法研究了无病平衡和地方病平衡的稳定性。此外,图形模拟还演示了延迟、疫苗接种 速率和分数阶的影响。结果表明,增加 疫苗接种 率会减少感染人口,并且与较低值的延迟相比,模型延迟参数的较大值会在固定时间产生较慢的疾病轨迹和较低的感染峰值。这反映了系统响应较慢,而不是实际情况。这些发现强调了疾病进展对延迟的敏感性。

papers.title: A rapidly developing outbreak of clade Ib mpox among gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men associated with severe proctitis, Northern Ireland, June 2026
papers.abstract: We describe a rapidly expanding clade Ib mpox outbreak among gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men in Northern Ireland. Following 12 months with no detected mpox cases, 22 confirmed cases were notified between 6 and 30 June 2026. Cases had a median age of 41 years; 19 had not travelled outside the United Kingdom or Ireland in the 21 days before symptom onset. The outbreak is characterised by severe anorectal disease and presentation to non-sexual health settings, including secondary care.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为高危人群(特别是具有性健康相关风险因素的人群)中针对 Ib 猴痘 分支的针对性 监测 和公共卫生应对措施提供信息。

analysis_zh.main_results: 暴发的特点是严重的肛门直肠疾病,2026年6月6日至30日期间报告了22例确诊病例,其中19例在症状出现前21天内没有英国或爱尔兰境外旅行史。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明 Ib 猴痘 分支具有独特的 暴发 模式,与严重的肛门直肠疾病和非性健康环境显着相关,这是在该人群中的一个新观察结果。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为高危人群(特别是具有性健康相关风险因素的人群)中针对 Ib 猴痘 分支的针对性 监测 和公共卫生应对措施提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于基于病例通报的描述性分析,由于缺乏详细的统计或因果分析,证据不充分。

E-mail: damian.kadylak@ gumed.edu.pl Introduction Mpox (formerly monkeypox) can result in residual scarring, particularly in visible or functionally sensitive areas such as the face. These scars may cause both aesthetic and functional impairment, yet the published data on their management remain extremely limited. We report a case of an extensive facial Mpox scar successfully treated with ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy. Case Presentation A 28-year-old Caucasian male presented in January 2023 with an extensive facial scar involving the skin of the chin and a defect of the lower lip. In October 2022, he had been diagnosed with Mpox and early syphilis. HIV infection was ruled out, and he had no chronic comorbidities. The diagnosis of Mpox was based on a typical clinical presentation; however, due to unavailability of molecular testing, it was not laboratory confirmed. Three months after the resolution of active ulcerations, extensive scarring developed, resulting in noticeable defor- mity of the lower-lip vermilion contour, mucosal dryness without functional impairment, and hypertrophy of the chin skin with itching and tightness (Figure 1). The patient underwent four sessions of ablative frac- tional CO2 laser therapy (power 20 W; dwell time 3000 μs; repeat interval 0.5 s) at monthly intervals. Posttreatment care included emollients and broad-spectrum photoprotection. No complication such as infection, prolonged erythema, or ­dyspigmentation was observed. Six months after the final session, the patient maintained a good aesthetic result with significantly reduced vermilion bor- der deformation and satisfactory patient-reported outcome. Discussion Residual scarring after Mpox infection represents an emerg- ing dermatological and reconstructive challenge. Early regis- try data suggested scarring in approximately 13 % of cases 2 Research Letter | Dermatol Pract Concept. 2026;16(3):7149 [1], while more recent prospective studies with follow-up of 12–23 months reported visible scars in 48–63% of patients [2,3]. Hyperpigmented, hypopigmented, and atrophic scars are most common, whereas hypertrophic or contractile scars may cause functional symptoms and aesthetic distress. Few reports have addressed post-Mpox scar manage- ment. Pimentel et al. described combined pulsed-dye and 1550 nm Er:Glass laser treatment of a penile scar with ­favorable results [4], while Raffaele et al. reported photody- namic and photobiomodulation therapy for an active facial ulceration [5]. However, standardized protocols for ablative or fractional laser therapy in Mpox scars are lacking, and treatment approaches are currently extrapolated from post- acne or post-burn scar management. Fractional CO2 laser therapy promotes dermal remodeling through controlled ablation and collagen regeneration. In this case, four sessions produced durable improvement without complications, supporting its potential as a safe, effective, and minimally invasive option for extensive post-Mpox scarring. Conclusion Ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy may offer an effective approach to improve both cosmetic and functional outcomes in post-Mpox scars. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the limited published data on managing residual scarring from Mpox infection, particularly in visible areas like the face, by reporting a case of successful treatment with ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a case report of a 28-year-old Caucasian male with extensive facial scarring following Mpox infection, treated with four sessions of ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy at monthly intervals.
analysis.methods: The patient underwent four sessions of ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy (power 20 W; dwell time 3000 μs; repeat interval 0.5 s) with post-treatment care including emollients and broad-spectrum photoprotection.
analysis.main_results: Six months after the final session, the patient maintained a good aesthetic result with significantly reduced vermilion border deformation and satisfactory patient-reported outcomes, with no complications such as infection, prolonged erythema, or dyspigmentation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy as a safe, effective, and minimally invasive option for extensive post-Mpox scarring, supporting its potential as a standardized treatment approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy can improve both cosmetic and functional outcomes in post-Mpox scars, providing a potential solution for an emerging dermatological and reconstructive challenge.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by the single-case design and lack of laboratory confirmation of Mpox diagnosis; further studies are required to establish standardized treatment parameters and evaluate long-term outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes the successful treatment of extensive facial scarring following Mpox infection in a 28-year-old male using ablative fractional CO2 laser therapy. Four monthly sessions resulted in significant aesthetic improvement and patient satisfaction without complications. The study highlights the emerging challenge of post-Mpox scarring and suggests laser therapy as a promising minimally invasive option, though standardized protocols and long-term data are needed.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究报告了 猴痘 消融点阵 CO2 激光治疗的成功案例,解决了已发表的关于处理 猴痘 感染残留疤痕的有限数据,特别是在面部等可见区域。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一名 28 岁白人男性的 病例报告,他在 猴痘 感染后面部留下了广泛的疤痕,每月接受四次消融点阵 CO2 激光治疗。
elements_zh.methods: 患者接受了四次消融点阵 CO2 激光治疗(功率 20 W;停留时间 3000 μs;重复间隔 0.5 s),并进行 治疗 后护理,包括润肤剂和广谱光保护。
elements_zh.main_results: 最后一次疗程后六个月,患者保持了良好的美学效果,朱红边界变形显着减少,患者报告的结果令人满意,没有感染、长时间红斑或色素沉着等并发症。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将烧蚀点阵 CO2 激光疗法解释为治疗 猴痘 后广泛疤痕的一种安全、有效和微创的选择,支持其作为标准化 治疗 方法的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,烧蚀点阵 CO2 激光疗法可以改善 猴痘 后疤痕的美容和功能结果,为新兴的皮肤病学和重建挑战提供潜在的解决方案。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 猴痘 诊断的单例设计和缺乏实验室确认,证据强度有限;需要进一步的研究来建立标准化的 治疗 参数并评估长期结果。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究报告了 猴痘 消融点阵 CO2 激光治疗的成功案例,解决了已发表的关于处理 猴痘 感染残留疤痕的有限数据,特别是在面部等可见区域。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一名 28 岁白人男性的 病例报告,他在 猴痘 感染后面部留下了广泛的疤痕,每月接受四次消融点阵 CO2 激光治疗。
analysis_zh.methods: 患者接受了四次消融点阵 CO2 激光治疗(功率 20 W;停留时间 3000 μs;重复间隔 0.5 s),并进行 治疗 后护理,包括润肤剂和广谱光保护。
analysis_zh.main_results: 最后一次疗程后六个月,患者保持了良好的美学效果,朱红边界变形显着减少,患者报告的结果令人满意,没有感染、长时间红斑或色素沉着等并发症。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将烧蚀点阵 CO2 激光疗法解释为治疗 猴痘 后广泛疤痕的一种安全、有效和微创的选择,支持其作为标准化 治疗 方法的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,烧蚀点阵 CO2 激光疗法可以改善 猴痘 后疤痕的美容和功能结果,为新兴的皮肤病学和重建挑战提供潜在的解决方案。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 猴痘 诊断的单例设计和缺乏实验室确认,证据强度有限;需要进一步的研究来建立标准化的 治疗 参数并评估长期结果。

papers.title: Rapid protection from lethal Orthopoxvirus infection following vaccination with mRNA-LNP encoding the Type I Interferon Binding Protein 2259797
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Orthopoxviruses (OPVs), such as monkeypox, pose ongoing public health threats, especially since the global herd immunity has declined following the cessation of routine smallpox vaccination. Current vaccine strategies have limitations due to safety and short-lived immunity. Most anti-viral vaccines aim to induce antibodies (Abs) that bind to structural viral proteins, preferentially those that can neutralize the viral particle. The Type I IFN-binding protein (IFN-I bp) is a highly conserved non-structural protein present in all OPVs, an immune evasion protein, and is essential for their pathogenicity. It has been previously shown that mice vaccinated with recombinant IFN-I bp or passively immunized with anti-IFN-I bp monoclonal antibodies (Abs), are protected from lethal challenge with the mouse OPV ectromelia virus (ECTV), a classic model for human smallpox and monkeypox infections. Methods We made mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding IFN-I bp. We evaluated Abs responses by ELISA, and protective efficacy by challenging the immunized mice with ECTV in the footpad or with the OPV vaccinia virus intranasally. Results We found that a single immunization of 5 ug of mRNA-LNPs encoding ECTV’s IFN-I bp induced much higher titers of IgG antibodies (as opposed to IgM) as early as six days post-immunization than control mRNA-LNP vaccines. Notably, vaccinated BALB/c and TLR9-deficient mice challenged with ECTV or VACV eight days post-immunization were fully protected from viral lethality. Conclusion These data indicate that the IFN-I bp is a promising antigen for OPV vaccines, particularly when rapid protection is crucial, such as during an epidemic. Ongoing studies aim to determine the mechanisms underlying rapid IgG induction. Funding Source grant Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Orthopoxviruses (OPVs), such as monkeypox, pose ongoing public health threats due to declining global herd immunity following the cessation of routine smallpox vaccination, and current vaccine strategies have limitations due to safety and short-lived immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the Type I IFN-binding protein in mice, assessing antibody responses by ELISA and protective efficacy against challenge with ectromelia virus (ECTV) or vaccinia virus.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed an mRNA-LNP vaccine encoding IFN-I bp, measured IgG and IgM antibody titers by ELISA, and challenged immunized BALB/c and TLR9-deficient mice with ECTV in the footpad or vaccinia virus intranasally to assess protection.
analysis.main_results: A single immunization with 5 μg of mRNA-LNPs encoding ECTV's IFN-I bp induced higher IgG antibody titers as early as six days post-immunization compared to controls, and vaccinated mice were fully protected from lethal challenge with ECTV or vaccinia virus eight days post-immunization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the IFN-I bp is a promising antigen for OPV vaccines, particularly when rapid protection is crucial, such as during an epidemic, as demonstrated by the full protection observed shortly after immunization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that mRNA-LNP vaccines targeting IFN-I bp could provide rapid protection against orthopoxvirus infections, offering a potential strategy for epidemic response where swift immunity is essential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study was conducted in mouse models and focused on a limited number of viral challenges; further research is needed to confirm efficacy in humans and understand the mechanisms of rapid IgG induction.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated an mRNA-LNP vaccine encoding the Type I IFN-binding protein (IFN-I bp) to provide rapid protection against orthopoxvirus infections. The researchers found that a single immunization induced high IgG antibody titers as early as six days post-vaccination and fully protected mice from lethal challenge with ectromelia virus or vaccinia virus just eight days after immunization. The results indicate that IFN-I bp is a promising antigen for OPV vaccines, particularly valuable during epidemics where rapid protection is critical. While the study demonstrates strong efficacy in mouse models, further research is needed to confirm these findings in humans and elucidate the mechanisms behind the rapid immune response.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 正痘病毒 (OPV),如猴痘,由于常规天花 疫苗接种 停止后全球群体免疫力下降,对公共卫生构成持续威胁,而当前的 疫苗 策略由于安全性和短期免疫力而存在局限性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了小鼠体内编码 I 型 IFN 结合蛋白的 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 (mRNA-LNP) 疫苗,通过 ELISA 评估抗体反应以及针对 ectromelia 病毒 (ECTV) 或牛痘病毒攻击的保护功效。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员开发了编码 IFN-I bp 的 mRNA-LNP 疫苗,通过 ELISA 测量 IgG 和 IgM 抗体滴度,并用足垫内的 ECTV 或鼻内痘苗病毒攻击免疫 BALB/c 和 TLR9 缺陷小鼠,以评估保护作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 与对照相比,用 5 μg 编码 ECTV IFN-I bp 的 mRNA-LNP 进行单次免疫,早在免疫后六天就诱导了更高的 IgG 抗体滴度,并且接种疫苗的小鼠在免疫后八天完全免受 ECTV 或牛痘病毒的致死攻击。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,IFN-I bp 是 OPV 疫苗 的一种有前途的抗原,特别是当快速保护至关重要时,例如在流行病期间,免疫接种后不久观察到的全面保护就证明了这一点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对 IFN-I bp 的 mRNA-LNP 疫苗 可以提供针对 正痘病毒 感染的快速保护,为快速免疫至关重要的流行病应对提供潜在策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究是在小鼠模型中进行的,并且重点关注有限数量的病毒挑战;需要进一步的研究来确认对人类的功效并了解快速 IgG 诱导的机制。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 正痘病毒 (OPV),如猴痘,由于常规天花 疫苗接种 停止后全球群体免疫力下降,对公共卫生构成持续威胁,而当前的 疫苗 策略由于安全性和短期免疫力而存在局限性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了小鼠体内编码 I 型 IFN 结合蛋白的 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 (mRNA-LNP) 疫苗,通过 ELISA 评估抗体反应以及针对 ectromelia 病毒 (ECTV) 或牛痘病毒攻击的保护功效。

papers.title: Immune Response to MVA-BN and Prior Smallpox Vaccination in People with HIV or at Risk for HIV Acquisition
papers.abstract: Little is known about the serologic response elicited by MVA-BN vaccination (JYNNEOS) against mpox in elderly individuals with or without HIV. In this study, we measured levels of antibody against orthopoxvirus in selected participants (n=114) with HIV or at risk for HIV acquisition, from the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study/Women's Interagency HIV Study Combined Cohort Study, who had no prior reported history of mpox. Participants reported MVA-BN vaccination history via questionnaires. Median age was 64 years, 24.6% were female, and 46% were HIV-seropositive. Twenty out of 114 participants received at least one dose of MVA-BN. We found that MVA-BN induced sustained IgG levels regardless of HIV status even up to one year. Birth before 1973 was correlated with higher IgG. MVA-BN unvaccinated individuals with HIV had lower IgG than those without HIV. Although limited by small sample size, our study is among the first to assess anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies specifically in a vulnerable, older population and stratified by HIV status.

papers.title: Examining the immune response of participants receiving Modified Vaccinia Ankara vaccine in Africa (MpoxVax AFRIVAC): a prospective cohort study - protocol.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mpox remains an ongoing global health concern, driven by an ongoing clade I outbreak in Central Africa, which has caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Despite deployment of the Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine, data on the durability of vaccine-induced immune responses remain limited, particularly in African populations, women and people with HIV, highlighting the need for context-specific immunogenicity data. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Mpox-Vax AFRIVAC is a prospective, multicentre observational cohort study conducted in Uganda, Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Adults eligible for MVA-BN vaccination for mpox prevention or who received a first dose within 28 days prior to enrolment are followed for 48 weeks. Serial blood samples are collected to quantify binding antibody responses and assess their durability over time. The primary outcomes are mean geometric MVA-BN-specific antibody titres at week 48 and the rate of antibody decay from week 6 to week 48. Secondary outcomes include antibody kinetics at intermediate time points, factors associated with immune responses, breakthrough infection and vaccine safety. Analyses will use descriptive and longitudinal statistical methods to evaluate immune response trajectories and associated host factors, including HIV status, age and sex. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study is conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, registered at the Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202601855406764) and publications will be in accordance with the recommendations of the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors. The study has received ethical approvals in Uganda, DRC and Tanzania. Approval for Uganda has been obtained from Uganda Virus Research Institute Research and Ethics Committee (GC/127/1062) and Uganda National Council for Science and Technology (HS5575ES), for DRC from the Institutional Committee of Health ethics (UCB/CIES/PB/001/2025) and for Tanzania from the National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR/HQ/R.8a/Vol.IX/5187). TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: PACTR202601855406764.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:猴痘 仍然是一个持续的全球健康问题,由中部非洲持续存在的 I 暴发 分支驱动,该分支已造成大量发病率和 死亡率。尽管部署了改良痘苗安卡拉-巴伐利亚北欧 (MVA-BN) 疫苗,但有关 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 持久性的数据仍然有限,特别是在非洲人群、妇女和艾滋病毒感染者中,这凸显了对具体情况免疫原性数据的需求。方法和分析:猴痘-Vax AFRIVAC 是一项在乌干达、坦桑尼亚和刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 进行的前瞻性、多中心观察性 队列研究 研究。对符合 MVA-BN 猴痘 预防资格的成人或在入组前 28 天内接受第一剂的成人进行为期 48 周的随访。收集连续血液样本以量化结合抗体反应并评估其随着时间的推移的耐久性。主要结果是第 48 周时的平均几何 MVA-BN 特异性抗体滴度以及从第 6 周到第 48 周的抗体衰减率。次要结果包括中间时间点的抗体动力学、与 免疫应答 相关的因素、突破性感染和 疫苗 安全性。分析将使用描述性和纵向统计方法来评估 免疫应答 轨迹和相关的 宿主 因素,包括 HIV 状况、年龄和性别。道德与传播:该研究是根据赫尔辛基宣言进行的,在泛非临床试验注册中心(PACTR202601855406764)注册,出版物将按照国际医学期刊编辑委员会的建议进行。该研究已获得乌干达、刚果民主共和国和坦桑尼亚的伦理批准。乌干达的批准已获得乌干达病毒研究所研究和伦理委员会(GC/127/1062)和乌干达国家科学技术委员会(HS5575ES)的批准,刚果民主共和国的批准已获得卫生伦理机构委员会(UCB/CIES/PB/001/2025)的批准,坦桑尼亚的批准已获得国家医学研究所(NIMR/HQ/R.8a/Vol.IX/5187)的批准。试用注册号:PACTR202601855406764。

papers.title: PregInPoxVac maternal protocol: a phase 3 trial evaluating maternal immunogenicity and safety of the MVA-BN vaccine in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mpox remains endemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with pregnant women at increased risk of severe disease and adverse outcomes. The WHO has called for data on mpox vaccination in high-risk groups, but no clinical trial has assessed the safety or immunogenicity of mpox vaccines in this population. The modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine, a third-generation, highly attenuated, non-replicating, live virus vaccine, has shown an excellent safety profile in adolescents and adults, including immunocompromised individuals, and is expected to be safe during pregnancy. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Pregnancy & Infancy mPox Vaccine study is a phase 3, open-label trial that aims to evaluate the safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity of the MVA-BN vaccine in pregnant and postpartum women in Boende, the DRC, compared with adults of the POX-MVA-045 study (NCT06549530) in DRC and Uganda. A total of 359 pregnant women (16-35 years old, in their second or third trimester of pregnancy) are being enrolled and randomised to receive the homologous MVA-BN vaccine regimen at a 28-day interval, with the first dose administered either before 32 weeks of gestation during pregnancy or within 72 hours postpartum (3:2 ratio randomisation). An additional, non-randomised group will receive post-exposure prophylaxis following confirmed mpox exposure. Primary immunogenicity analyses will assess the non-inferiority of neutralising antibody titres in pregnant women compared with those in non-pregnant adults. Primary safety analyses will compare reactogenicity in pregnant women to that observed in adults and safety in pregnant women to safety observed in adults and women vaccinated in the immediate postpartum period. Secondary analysis will evaluate neutralising antibody titres and total binding antibody concentrations over time for pregnant and postpartum women compared with adults and each other. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The trial integrates ancillary care pathways, local capacity building and formative workshops that co-developed research tools. analysis.summary_en: This phase 3 trial evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of the MVA-BN mpox vaccine in pregnant and postpartum women in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Primary results will assess non-inferiority of neutralising antibody titres, while secondary analyses will track antibody levels over time. The study's findings could inform future vaccination strategies for pregnant women, but its evidence is moderate due to being based on an abstract-only report and limited geographic scope.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘 在刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 仍然流行,孕妇患严重疾病和不良后果的风险增加。WHO已呼吁提供猴痘 疫苗在高危人群中的数据,但尚无临床试验评估猴痘 疫苗在该人群中的安全性或免疫原性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 刚果民主共和国博恩代正在进行一项 3 期开放标签试验,以评估 MVA-BN 疫苗 在孕妇和产后妇女中的安全性、反应原性和免疫原性,与刚果民主共和国和乌干达 POX-MVA-045 研究的成人相比。共有 359 名孕妇(16-35 岁,怀孕中期或晚期)被招募并随机接受同源 MVA-BN 疫苗 方案,间隔 28 天。
elements_zh.methods: 妊娠和婴儿期 猴痘 疫苗 研究是一项 3 期开放标签试验,旨在与刚果民主共和国和乌干达的 POX-MVA-045 研究 (NCT06549530) 的成人相比,评估 MVA-BN 疫苗 在刚果博恩代孕妇和产后妇女中的安全性、反应原性和免疫原性。
elements_zh.main_results: 初步免疫原性分析将评估孕妇中和抗体滴度与非妊娠成人相比的非劣效性。二次分析将评估孕妇和产后妇女与成人和彼此之间随时间变化的中和抗体滴度和总结合抗体浓度。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了有关 MVA-BN 疫苗 在孕妇中的安全性和免疫原性的新数据,解决了针对这一高危人群开发 猴痘 疫苗 的关键知识差距。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为孕妇制定 猴痘 疫苗接种 策略提供信息,有助于改善刚果民主共和国和其他流行地区的 监测、预防和公共卫生应对措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注单一地理位置且缺乏长期随访数据而受到限制。证据是温和的,因为它基于仅摘要的报告。

papers.abstract_zh: 简介:猴痘 在刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 仍然流行,孕妇患严重疾病和不良后果的风险增加。WHO已呼吁提供猴痘 疫苗在高危人群中的数据,但尚无临床试验评估猴痘 疫苗在该人群中的安全性或免疫原性。改良痘苗安卡拉-巴伐利亚北欧 (MVA-BN) 疫苗 是第三代、高度减毒、非复制的活病毒 疫苗,在青少年和成人(包括免疫功能低下的个体)中表现出出色的安全性,预计在怀孕期间也是安全的。方法和分析:妊娠期和婴儿期 猴痘 疫苗 研究是一项 3 期开放标签试验,旨在评估 MVA-BN 疫苗 在刚果民主共和国博恩德孕妇和产后妇女中的安全性、反应原性和免疫原性,与 POX-MVA-045 研究的成人相比(NCT06549530) 位于刚果民主共和国和乌干达。共有 359 名孕妇(16-35 岁,怀孕中期或晚期)被招募并随机接受同源 MVA-BN 疫苗 方案,间隔 28 天,第一剂在怀孕期间妊娠 32 周前或产后 72 小时内给药(3:2 比例随机化)。另外一个非随机组将在确认 猴痘 暴露后接受暴露后预防。初步免疫原性分析将评估孕妇中和抗体滴度与非妊娠成人相比的非劣效性。初步安全性分析将比较孕妇的反应原性与成人中观察到的反应原性,以及孕妇的安全性与成人和产后立即接种疫苗的女性观察到的安全性。二次分析将评估孕妇和产后妇女与成人和彼此之间随时间变化的中和抗体滴度和总结合抗体浓度。伦理与传播:该试验整合了辅助护理途径、当地能力建设和共同开发研究工具的形成研讨会。获得了刚果民主共和国和比利时机构和国家审查委员会的伦理批准。结果将与当地社区、国家利益相关者和全球卫生机构分享。试用注册号:NCT06844500 和 PACTR202511506487215。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了有关 MVA-BN 疫苗 在孕妇中的安全性和免疫原性的新数据,解决了针对这一高危人群开发 猴痘 疫苗 的关键知识差距。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为孕妇制定 猴痘 疫苗接种 策略提供信息,有助于改善刚果民主共和国和其他流行地区的 监测、预防和公共卫生应对措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注单一地理位置且缺乏长期随访数据而受到限制。证据是温和的,因为它基于仅摘要的报告。

papers.title: Outbreak preparedness for women and girls in low- and middle-income countries: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Infectious disease outbreaks ("outbreaks") pose heightened gender-based violence (GBV) risk for women and girls. However, little is known about the integration of GBV and gender-informed programming within outbreak preparedness and response in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). METHODS: This qualitative study draws on in-depth interviews with ten public health practitioners with experience supporting infectious disease outbreak preparedness and response in LMICs. Participants represented intergovernmental organizations and worked across multiple outbreak contexts, including Ebola, COVID-19, Mpox, Zika, and Cholera, in diverse geographic settings. Interviews examined barriers, gaps, successes, and opportunities for integrating gender-informed programming and GBV considerations into outbreak preparedness and response. Authors employed thematic content analysis with a mixed inductive and deductive coding approach to analyze data. RESULTS: Four major themes emerged. First, participants described the persistent normalization of excluding gender and GBV considerations from outbreak response, driven by competing priorities and inadequate funding. Second, they identified insufficient community engagement and localization, emphasizing that responses often fail to account for existing gender norms, community priorities, and local expertise. Third, participants highlighted fragmented coordination across sectors and organizations, advocating for stronger partnerships with women-led organizations (WLOs), improved collaboration, and more gender-balanced leadership. Finally, they emphasized the need to better institutionalize lessons learned and operationalize existing evidence to strengthen preparedness and support more effective, gender-informed responses during future outbreaks. CONCLUSIONS: To strengthen gender integration in global outbreak response, we recommend embedding GBV risk mitigation throughout response planning, improving cross-sector coordination and gender-balanced leadership, strengthening partnerships with local WLOs, and adopting flexible long-term funding mechanisms. Integrating gender-informed approaches into outbreak preparedness is essential to protecting women and girls, strengthening community resilience, and improving the effectiveness and sustainability of public health responses in LMICs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the persistent gap in integrating gender-based violence (GBV) and gender-informed programming into outbreak preparedness and response in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). It highlights the heightened GBV risks faced by women and girls during infectious disease outbreaks as a critical public-health problem necessitating targeted preparedness strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This qualitative study conducted in-depth interviews with ten public health practitioners experienced in supporting infectious disease outbreak preparedness and response in LMICs. Participants represented intergovernmental organizations and worked across multiple outbreak contexts, including Ebola, COVID-19, Mpox, Zika, and Cholera, in diverse geographic settings.
analysis.methods: The authors employed thematic content analysis using a mixed inductive and deductive coding approach to analyze interview data. Interviews were designed to examine barriers, gaps, successes, and opportunities for integrating gender-informed programming and GBV considerations into outbreak preparedness and response.
analysis.main_results: Four major themes emerged from the interviews: persistent exclusion of gender and GBV considerations due to competing priorities and inadequate funding; insufficient community engagement and localization; fragmented coordination across sectors; and the need to institutionalize lessons learned and operationalize existing evidence for future preparedness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that gender integration in outbreak response remains underprioritized despite its critical role in protecting women and girls and strengthening community resilience. They emphasize the novelty of centering practitioner perspectives to identify actionable gaps and opportunities for systemic improvement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that embedding GBV risk mitigation into response planning, improving cross-sector coordination, strengthening partnerships with women-led organizations, and adopting flexible long-term funding mechanisms could enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of public health responses in LMICs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size of ten practitioners and reliance on qualitative methods, which may not capture the full range of barriers or successes across diverse contexts. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of quantitative validation or broader stakeholder perspectives.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explores barriers to integrating gender-based violence (GBV) and gender-informed programming into outbreak preparedness and response in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Through in-depth interviews with ten public health practitioners experienced in outbreaks such as Ebola, COVID-19, Mpox, Zika, and Cholera, the authors identify four major themes: persistent exclusion of gender considerations due to competing priorities and funding gaps, insufficient community engagement, fragmented coordination, and the need to institutionalize lessons learned. The study emphasizes the critical role of gender integration in protecting women and girls and strengthening community resilience, recommending systemic improvements such as embedding GBV risk mitigation into planning, enhancing cross-sector partnerships, and adopting flexible funding mechanisms. However, the small sample size and qualitative design limit the generalizability of findings, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 暴发 低收入和中等收入国家妇女和女童的准备:一项定性研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Infectious disease outbreaks ("outbreaks") pose heightened gender-based violence (GBV) risk for women and girls. However, little is known about the integration of GBV and gender-informed programming within outbreak preparedness and response in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). METHODS: This qualitative study draws on in-depth interviews with ten public health practitioners with experience supporting infectious disease outbreak preparedness and response in LMICs. Participants represented intergovernmental organizations and worked across multiple outbreak contexts, including Ebola, COVID-19, Mpox, Zika, and Cholera, in diverse geographic settings. Interviews examined barriers, gaps, successes, and opportunities for integrating gender-informed programming and GBV considerations into outbreak preparedness and response. Authors employed thematic content analysis with a mixed inductive and deductive coding approach to analyze data. RESULTS: Four major themes emerged. First, participants described the persistent normalization of excluding gender and GBV considerations from outbreak response, driven by competing priorities and inadequate funding. Second, they identified insufficient community engagement and localization, emphasizing that responses often fail to account for existing gender norms, community priorities, and local expertise. Third, participants highlighted fragmented coordination across sectors and organizations, advocating for stronger partnerships with women-led organizations (WLOs), improved collaboration, and more gender-balanced leadership. Finally, they emphasized the need to better institutionalize lessons learned and operationalize existing evidence to strengthen preparedness and support more effective, gender-informed responses during future outbreaks. CONCLUSIONS: To strengthen gender integration in global outbreak response, we recommend embedding GBV risk mitigation throughout response planning, improving cross-sector coordination and gender-balanced leadership, strengthening partnerships with local WLOs, and adopting flexible long-term funding mechanisms. Integrating gender-informed approaches into outbreak preparedness is essential to protecting women and girls, strengthening community resilience, and improving the effectiveness and sustainability of public health responses in LMICs.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:传染病 暴发(“暴发”)给妇女和女童带来更高的性别暴力 (GBV) 风险。然而,人们对将 GBV 和性别知情规划纳入低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 的 暴发 准备和响应中的情况知之甚少。方法:这项定性研究借鉴了对 10 名公共卫生从业者的深入访谈,他们具有支持中低收入国家传染病 暴发 准备和应对的经验。参与者代表政府间组织,并在多个 暴发 背景下工作,包括埃博拉、COVID-19、猴痘、寨卡和霍乱,在不同的地理环境中。访谈考察了将性别知情规划和 GBV 考虑因素纳入 暴发 准备和响应的障碍、差距、成功和机会。作者采用主题内容分析和混合归纳和演绎编码方法来分析数据。结果:出现了四个主要主题。首先,与会者描述了在优先事项相互竞争和资金不足的推动下,将性别和 GBV 考虑因素排除在 暴发 响应之外的持续正常化。其次,他们发现社区参与和本地化不足,强调应对措施往往未能考虑到现有的性别规范、社区优先事项和当地专业知识。第三,与会者强调了跨部门和组织的分散协调,主张与女性领导的组织(WLO)建立更强有力的伙伴关系,改善协作,并实现更加性别平衡的领导力。最后,他们强调需要更好地将经验教训制度化并运用现有证据,以加强准备工作并支持在未来的 暴发 期间采取更有效、性别信息丰富的应对措施。结论:为了加强全球 暴发 应对措施中的性别融合,我们建议将 GBV 风险缓解纳入整个应对计划中,改善跨部门协调和性别平衡领导力,加强与当地 WLO 的伙伴关系,并采用灵活的长期融资机制。将性别知情方法纳入 暴发 准备工作对于保护妇女和女童、增强社区复原力以及提高中低收入国家公共卫生应对措施的有效性和可持续性至关重要。

papers.title: Digital Health for Pandemic Preparedness: A Critical Review of Innovations, Equity Gaps, and Governance in Infectious Disease Surveillance
papers.abstract: Context: Recent infectious disease emergencies, including SARS-CoV-2, mpox (2022 - 2024), highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in US dairy cattle (2024 - 2025), and the Marburg virus in Rwanda (2024), have strained traditional surveillance systems. Digital health has been proposed as a paradigm shift; however, most reviews have focused on diagnostic accuracy while neglecting equity and governance. Evidence Acquisition: We conducted a structured thematic narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature published from January 2010 to March 2025, reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from February 5 to 18, 2025. Search keywords combined three concept blocks: (1) Digital-health technologies (artificial intelligence, machine learning, mHealth, eHealth, telemedicine, electronic health records, wearables, wastewater surveillance, genomic surveillance, natural-language processing); (2) infectious diseases (outbreak, pandemic, epidemic, COVID-19, Ebola, Zika, mpox, influenza, antimicrobial resistance, Marburg); and (3) public-health functions (surveillance, detection, forecasting, contact tracing, governance, equity). Full Boolean syntax is provided. Records were deduplicated in EndNote X20 and screened by 2 blinded reviewers in Rayyan (Cohen κ = 0.81). Empirical studies were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, and reviews were appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The synthesis followed Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and was interpreted through sociotechnical systems and data justice lenses. Results: Of 1498 records, 142 studies met the inclusion criteria; 48% (69/142) were rated as high quality. The evidence base was heavily skewed regionally (high-income countries [HICs], 41%; sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia, 19%). No technology was universally superior. Artificial intelligence (AI) studies were concentrated in HICs (18/32, 56%), whereas short-message-service (SMS) mHealth studies were concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs; 15/25, 60%). Recurring barriers included algorithmic bias, fragmented interoperability, donor-dependent sustainability, and slow benefit-sharing of pathogen data with LMICs. Conclusions: Across 142 included studies the synthesis supports a measured conclusion: Digital health is necessary but not sufficient for pandemic preparedness. The patterns most consistently observed in the evidence — regional skew, recurring governance failures, donor-dependent sustainability, and design choices that determine equity outcomes — together indicate that equity, sustainability, and accountability are constituents of effectiveness rather than obstacles to it. The binding constraint is increasingly political and institutional will rather than analytic uncertainty.

papers.title_zh: 应对流行病准备的数字健康:对传染病创新、公平差距和治理的批判性回顾 监测
papers.source_body_en: Context: Recent infectious disease emergencies, including SARS-CoV-2, mpox (2022 - 2024), highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in US dairy cattle (2024 - 2025), and the Marburg virus in Rwanda (2024), have strained traditional surveillance systems. Digital health has been proposed as a paradigm shift; however, most reviews have focused on diagnostic accuracy while neglecting equity and governance. Evidence Acquisition: We conducted a structured thematic narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature published from January 2010 to March 2025, reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from February 5 to 18, 2025. Search keywords combined three concept blocks: (1) Digital-health technologies (artificial intelligence, machine learning, mHealth, eHealth, telemedicine, electronic health records, wearables, wastewater surveillance, genomic surveillance, natural-language processing); (2) infectious diseases (outbreak, pandemic, epidemic, COVID-19, Ebola, Zika, mpox, influenza, antimicrobial resistance, Marburg); and (3) public-health functions (surveillance, detection, forecasting, contact tracing, governance, equity). Full Boolean syntax is provided. Records were deduplicated in EndNote X20 and screened by 2 blinded reviewers in Rayyan (Cohen κ = 0.81). Empirical studies were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, and reviews were appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The synthesis followed Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and was interpreted through sociotechnical systems and data justice lenses. Results: Of 1498 records, 142 studies met the inclusion criteria; 48% (69/142) were rated as high quality. The evidence base was heavily skewed regionally (high-income countries [HICs], 41%; sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia, 19%). No technology was universally superior. Artificial intelligence (AI) studies were concentrated in HICs (18/32, 56%), whereas short-message-service (SMS) mHealth studies were concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs; 15/25, 60%). Recurring barriers included algorithmic bias, fragmented interoperability, donor-dependent sustainability, and slow benefit-sharing of pathogen data with LMICs. Conclusions: Across 142 included studies the synthesis supports a measured conclusion: Digital health is necessary but not sufficient for pandemic preparedness. The patterns most consistently observed in the evidence — regional skew, recurring governance failures, donor-dependent sustainability, and design choices that determine equity outcomes — together indicate that equity, sustainability, and accountability are constituents of effectiveness rather than obstacles to it. The binding constraint is increasingly political and institutional will rather than analytic uncertainty.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:最近的传染病紧急事件,包括SARS-CoV-2、猴痘(2022-2024年)、美国奶牛中的高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)(2024-2025年)以及卢旺达的马尔堡病毒(2024年),都对传统的监测系统造成了压力。数字健康已被提出作为一种范式转变;然而,大多数评论都集中在诊断准确性上,而忽视了公平性和治理。证据获取:我们进行了一项结构化的主题叙事综述,涵盖了从2010年1月至2025年3月发表的同行评议文献和灰色文献,并按照PRISMA 2020和PRISMA-ScR进行报告。于2025年2月5日至18日检索了PubMed、Scopus和Web of Science。搜索关键词结合了三个概念块:(1)数字健康技术(人工智能、机器学习、移动健康、电子健康、远程医疗、电子健康记录、可穿戴设备、废水监测、基因组监测、自然语言处理);(2)传染病(暴发、大流行、流行病、COVID-19、埃博拉、寨卡、猴痘、流感、抗菌素耐药性、马尔堡);(3)公共卫生功能(监测、检测、预测、接触者追踪、治理、公平性)。提供了完整的布尔语法。在EndNote X20中去重记录,并由2名盲审评审人员在Rayyan中进行筛选(Cohen κ = 0.81)。使用混合方法评估工具2018评估实证研究,使用Joanna Briggs Institute清单评估综述。综合分析遵循Braun和Clarke的反身主题分析,并通过社会技术系统和数据正义视角进行解释。结果:在1498条记录中,142项研究符合纳入标准;48%(69/142)被评为高质量。证据基础在区域分布上严重偏向(高收入国家[HICs],41%;撒哈拉以南非洲或南亚,19%)。没有一种技术具有普遍优越性。人工智能(AI)研究集中在高收入国家(32项中的18项,56%),而短信服务(SMS)移动健康研究则集中在低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs;25项中的15项,60%)。反复出现的障碍包括算法偏见、碎片化的互操作性、依赖捐助者的可持续性,以及与低收入和中等收入国家分享病原体数据的缓慢利益共享。结论:在142项纳入研究的综合分析支持下,我们得出一个谨慎的结论:数字健康对于大流行防范是必要但不充分的。证据中最一致观察到的模式——区域偏向、反复出现的治理失败、依赖捐助者的可持续性,以及决定公平性结果的设计选择——共同表明,公平性、可持续性和问责制是有效性的组成部分,而非障碍。日益受到限制的是政治和制度意愿,而非分析不确定性。

papers.title: Cross-Outbreak Transfer Learning Under Data/Label Scarcity: Foundation ML model for epidemiology
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Early outbreak line lists are high-value but difficult machine-learning data. Their schemas, missingness patterns, case definitions, and confirmation processes change across pathogens and jurisdictions. A model pretrained on one outbreak can therefore transfer harmful shortcuts rather than reusable epidemiological structure. Methods: We developed OBFM-SafeEnsemble, a guarded cross-outbreak learning framework. A historical 2022 mpox line list (69,595 records) supplied source self-supervision and source coefficient priors; a live 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease Ebola line list (2,900 records) was the primary target; and a 24-record hantavirus line list was used only as a pipeline stress test. The endpoint was confirmation status. Direct laboratory, confirmation, outcome, post-confirmation care, provenance, and identifier fields were excluded to reduce leakage. OBFM-Lite first evaluated masked-token pretraining and continual unlabeled adaptation. OBFM-SafePrior then regularized a new Ebola head toward source-learned token effects and activated transfer only when validation AUROC exceeded a prespecified gain threshold. OBFM-SafeEnsemble trained a small library of disease-only and source-prior heads and selected either the best head, a top-N average, or a convex blend, always retaining a disease-only fallback. Results: Source masked-token pretraining improved in-domain mpox Transformer AUROC from 0.839 to 0.851. Continual unlabeled adaptation improved Ebola zero-shot AUROC from 0.487 to 0.523, but absolute transfer remained weak. At 64 labeled Ebola records, SafePrior improved AUROC from 0.524 to 0.664 and AUPRC from 0.660 to 0.731. SafeEnsemble achieved AUROC values of 0.662, 0.656, 0.687, 0.682, and 0.667 at 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 labels, respectively. Relative to matched disease-only models, AUROC gains were +0.068, +0.082, +0.235, +0.064, and +0.015; AUPRC gains were +0.042, +0.067, +0.160, +0.074, and +0.033. Interpretation: Positive cross-outbreak transfer was achievable under severe label scarcity only after source knowledge was treated as optional, target-validated regularization and averaged across low-variance candidate heads.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background: Early outbreak line lists are high-value but difficult machine-learning data. Their schemas, missingness patterns, case definitions, and confirmation processes change across pathogens and jurisdictions. A model pretrained on one outbreak can therefore transfer harmful shortcuts rather than reusable epidemiological structure. Methods: We developed OBFM-SafeEnsemble, a guarded cross-outbreak learning framework. A historical 2022 mpox line list (69,595 records) supplied source self-supervision and source coefficient priors; a live 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease Ebola line list (2,900 records) was the primary target; and a 24-record hantavirus line list was used only as a pipeline stress test. The endpoint was confirmation status. Direct laboratory, confirmation, outcome, post-confirmation care, provenance, and identifier fields were excluded to reduce leakage. OBFM-Lite first evaluated masked-token pretraining and continual unlabeled adaptation. OBFM-SafePrior then regularized a new Ebola head toward source-learned token effects and activated transfer only when validation AUROC exceeded a prespecified gain threshold. OBFM-SafeEnsemble trained a small library of disease-only and source-prior heads and selected either the best head, a top-N average, or a convex blend, always retaining a disease-only fallback. Results: Source masked-token pretraining improved in-domain mpox Transformer AUROC from 0.839 to 0.851. Continual unlabeled adaptation improved Ebola zero-shot AUROC from 0.487 to 0.523, but absolute transfer remained weak. At 64 labeled Ebola records, SafePrior improved AUROC from 0.524 to 0.664 and AUPRC from 0.660 to 0.731. SafeEnsemble achieved AUROC values of 0.662, 0.656, 0.687, 0.682, and 0.667 at 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 labels, respectively. Relative to matched disease-only models, AUROC gains were +0.068, +0.082, +0.235, +0.064, and +0.015; AUPRC gains were +0.042, +0.067, +0.160, +0.074, and +0.033. Interpretation: Positive cross-outbreak transfer was achievable under severe label scarcity only after source knowledge was treated as optional, target-validated regularization and averaged across low-variance candidate heads.

papers.title: Directing Defense: ZBP1 Activation during MPXV Infection 2309240
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Monkeypox virus (MPXV) remains a global health concern due to the recent outbreak that exhibited an increase in human transmission. This highlights the need to better understand the viral host interactions to identify novel antiviral strategies. Z-DNA Binding Protein-1 (ZBP1) is an innate immune sensor that can recognize Z-ribonucleic acid (Z-RNA). Z-RNA is a novel pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP), produced during early viral replication, and can be sensed by ZBP1. Activation of ZBP1 can initiate antiviral signaling pathways that can restrict viral replication and limit disease progression. However, whether ZBP1 contributes to controlling MPXV replication and spread remains a significant gap in knowledge. Methods Wild-type (WT) and ZBP1-knockout (ZBP1-KO) bone-marrow-derived-macrophages (BMDMs) were infected with MPXV to determine the viral replication and spread using single-step and multi-step growth curves. Viral titers were quantified by plaque assay, and viral gene expression was measured by RT-qPCR. In vivo, WT and ZBP1-KO mice were infected intranasally with MPXV, mimicking the respiratory route transmission. Lung tissues were collected at 1, 3, and 5 days post-infection (dpi) to quantify viral titers and viral gene expression. Results Findings reveal that ZBP1 deficiency results in increased MPXV replication and spread during single and multi-step growth curves of MPXV infection, as indicated by an elevated viral titer. Increased viral gene expression was also observed in lung tissues from ZBP1-KO at 3dpi, suggesting an antiviral role for the host ZBP1 during MPXV infection. Conclusion Together, these results demonstrate that ZBP1 plays an antiviral role during MPXV infection. However, further studies are needed to define the host defense pathways involved, such as TBK1 and NF-κB signaling. Understanding how ZBP1 restricts MPXV as Z-RNA is produced during early MPXV infection can help address a significant gap in understanding the viral host interactions. Funding Source GR00012379 Topic Categories Innate Immune Responses and Host Defense: Molecular Mechanisms (INM)

papers.title_zh: 指导防御:MPXV 感染期间 ZBP1 激活 2309240
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Monkeypox virus (MPXV) remains a global health concern due to the recent outbreak that exhibited an increase in human transmission. This highlights the need to better understand the viral host interactions to identify novel antiviral strategies. Z-DNA Binding Protein-1 (ZBP1) is an innate immune sensor that can recognize Z-ribonucleic acid (Z-RNA). Z-RNA is a novel pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP), produced during early viral replication, and can be sensed by ZBP1. Activation of ZBP1 can initiate antiviral signaling pathways that can restrict viral replication and limit disease progression. However, whether ZBP1 contributes to controlling MPXV replication and spread remains a significant gap in knowledge. Methods Wild-type (WT) and ZBP1-knockout (ZBP1-KO) bone-marrow-derived-macrophages (BMDMs) were infected with MPXV to determine the viral replication and spread using single-step and multi-step growth curves. Viral titers were quantified by plaque assay, and viral gene expression was measured by RT-qPCR. In vivo, WT and ZBP1-KO mice were infected intranasally with MPXV, mimicking the respiratory route transmission. Lung tissues were collected at 1, 3, and 5 days post-infection (dpi) to quantify viral titers and viral gene expression. Results Findings reveal that ZBP1 deficiency results in increased MPXV replication and spread during single and multi-step growth curves of MPXV infection, as indicated by an elevated viral titer. Increased viral gene expression was also observed in lung tissues from ZBP1-KO at 3dpi, suggesting an antiviral role for the host ZBP1 during MPXV infection. Conclusion Together, these results demonstrate that ZBP1 plays an antiviral role during MPXV infection. However, further studies are needed to define the host defense pathways involved, such as TBK1 and NF-κB signaling. Understanding how ZBP1 restricts MPXV as Z-RNA is produced during early MPXV infection can help address a significant gap in understanding the viral host interactions. Funding Source GR00012379 Topic Categories Innate Immune Responses and Host Defense: Molecular Mechanisms (INM)

papers.abstract: กรมควบคุมโรค ได้รับรายงานเหตุการณ์ โรค และภัยสุขภาพที่สําคัญ ผ่านโปรแกรมการตรวจสอบข่าวการระบาด กรมควบคุมโรค จากเครือข่ายงานสาธารณสุขทั่วประเทศ ดังนี้ สถานการณ์ในประเทศ 1. โรคฝีดาษวานร (Mpox) clade I/Ib จํานวน 5 เหตุการณ์ ในกรุงเทพมหานคร และจังหวัดปทุมธานี 2. การประเมินความเสี่ยงของการระบาดของโรคติดเชื้อสเตร็ปโตคอคคัสซูอิส ในประเทศไทย เดือนกรกฎาคม–สิงหาคม 2569 ในพื้นที่เขตสุขภาพ 1 2 และ 3 สถานการณ์ต่างประเทศ สาธารณรัฐประชาธิปไตยประชาชนลาวพบผู้ป่วยโปลิโอจากเชื้อวัคซีนกลายพันธุ์ (VDPV1) รายใหม่

source_records.abstract: กรมควบคุมโรค ได้รับรายงานเหตุการณ์ โรค และภัยสุขภาพที่สําคัญ ผ่านโปรแกรมการตรวจสอบข่าวการระบาด กรมควบคุมโรค จากเครือข่ายงานสาธารณสุขทั่วประเทศ ดังนี้ สถานการณ์ในประเทศ 1. โรคฝีดาษวานร (Mpox) clade I/Ib จํานวน 5 เหตุการณ์ ในกรุงเทพมหานคร และจังหวัดปทุมธานี 2. การประเมินความเสี่ยงของการระบาดของโรคติดเชื้อสเตร็ปโตคอคคัสซูอิส ในประเทศไทย เดือนกรกฎาคม–สิงหาคม 2569 ในพื้นที่เขตสุขภาพ 1 2 และ 3 สถานการณ์ต่างประเทศ สาธารณรัฐประชาธิปไตยประชาชนลาวพบผู้ป่วยโปลิโอจากเชื้อวัคซีนกลายพันธุ์ (VDPV1) รายใหม่

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to monitor and report significant health events and outbreaks in Thailand through the epidemic news surveillance program.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The surveillance program collected reports from public health networks nationwide, focusing on domestic and international health events.
analysis.methods: The assessment involved evaluating the risk of Streptococcus suis infection in Thailand during July-August 2569 in health zones 1, 2, and 3.
analysis.main_results: Five cases of Mpox clade I/Ib were reported in Bangkok and Pathum Thani province; a new case of VDPV1 poliomyelitis was found in Laos.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight ongoing Mpox transmission in Thailand and the emergence of vaccine-derived poliovirus in neighboring countries.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The data supports enhanced surveillance for Mpox and poliovirus to guide public health responses and prevent further spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to reported events and lacks detailed epidemiological analysis; confidence is moderate due to the abstract-only scope.

analysis.summary_en: This report summarizes significant health events in Thailand for the week of July 29, 2569, through the epidemic news surveillance program. Five cases of Mpox clade I/Ib were reported in Bangkok and Pathum Thani, while a new case of VDPV1 poliomyelitis was identified in Laos. The study assessed the risk of Streptococcus suis infection in Thailand's health zones 1-3. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance of Mpox and poliovirus to inform public health interventions and prevent further transmission.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过流行病新闻监测节目监测和报告泰国的重大健康事件和暴发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 监测 项目收集了全国公共卫生网络的报告,重点关注国内和国际健康事件。
elements_zh.methods: 该评估涉及评估 2569 年 7 月至 8 月期间泰国 1、2 和 3 卫生区猪链球菌感染的风险。
elements_zh.main_results: 曼谷和巴吞他尼府报告了 5 例 猴痘 进化枝 I/Ib 病例;老挝发现一例新的VDPV1型脊髓灰质炎病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了泰国正在进行的 猴痘 传播 以及邻国出现的源自 疫苗 的脊髓灰质炎病毒。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该数据支持 猴痘 和脊髓灰质炎病毒的增强型 监测,以指导公共卫生应对措施并防止进一步传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于报告的事件,缺乏详细的流行病学分析;由于仅限抽象范围,置信度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过流行病新闻监测节目监测和报告泰国的重大健康事件和暴发。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 监测 项目收集了全国公共卫生网络的报告,重点关注国内和国际健康事件。
analysis_zh.methods: 该评估涉及评估 2569 年 7 月至 8 月期间泰国 1、2 和 3 卫生区猪链球菌感染的风险。
analysis_zh.main_results: 曼谷和巴吞他尼府报告了 5 例 猴痘 进化枝 I/Ib 病例;老挝发现一例新的VDPV1型脊髓灰质炎病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了泰国正在进行的 猴痘 传播 以及邻国出现的源自 疫苗 的脊髓灰质炎病毒。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该数据支持 猴痘 和脊髓灰质炎病毒的增强型 监测,以指导公共卫生应对措施并防止进一步传播。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于报告的事件,缺乏详细的流行病学分析;由于仅限抽象范围,置信度中等。

papers.full_text: Abstract Skin diseases have a variety of causes, including exposure to chemicals, sunlight, viruses, bacteria, and other factors. Classification of skin diseases is essential because of their similar symptoms, such as red rashes, itching, and burning. The similar symptoms of the diseases make it difficult to distinguish them visually. This research aims to classify skin diseases using a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. The dataset used is MSLD v2.0, which is skin disease image data with 6 classes, namely monkeypox, cowpox, chickenpox, measles, HFMD, and healthy. Hybrid CNN is an integration between the CNN model and machine learning methods. This research uses three CNN models, namely EfficientNet, DenseNet, and ResNet, as feature extraction. The classification methods used include logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. Data augmentation is also applied to increase data variation. The highest performance results are obtained when using ResNet as a feature extraction and logistic regression as a classification method after going through the data augmentation process with an accuracy of 82% and a macro f1-score of 80%, which showed high performance in skin disease detection. Hybrid CNN with machine learning method shows the ability to feature extraction of skin disease images and achieves optimal performance. analysis.study_design_and_population: This research used the MSLD v2.0 dataset, which contains skin disease images with 6 classes: monkeypox, cowpox, chickenpox, measles, HFMD, and healthy.
analysis.methods: The study employed a hybrid CNN approach integrating CNN models (EfficientNet, DenseNet, and ResNet) for feature extraction with machine learning methods (logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost) for classification, along with data augmentation.
analysis.main_results: The highest performance was achieved using ResNet for feature extraction and logistic regression for classification after data augmentation, with an accuracy of 82% and a macro f1-score of 80%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The hybrid CNN with machine learning demonstrated strong ability in feature extraction of skin disease images and achieved optimal performance for skin disease detection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of automated diagnostic tools for skin diseases, including monkeypox, potentially improving early detection and classification in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as the study was conducted on a specific dataset with limited classes, and the performance metrics, while high, may not generalize to all populations or skin disease types.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method to classify skin diseases, including monkeypox, using the MSLD v2.0 dataset. The approach integrated CNN models (EfficientNet, DenseNet, and ResNet) for feature extraction with machine learning methods (logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost) for classification, along with data augmentation. The highest performance was achieved with ResNet and logistic regression, achieving 82% accuracy and 80% macro f1-score. The hybrid method demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities and optimal performance for skin disease detection, potentially improving automated diagnostic tools for clinical use.
